answer: To blunt sybil attacks, tie influence to an escalating stake spiral: an agent's first identity posts a small bond, but each additional identity funded by the same backer multiplies the required deposit by a fixed factor, so attack costs climb exponentially rather than linearly. Honest agents pool savings into a shared haven reserve that insures legitimate work and pays bounties for exposed sockpuppets. Caught offenders forfeit their entire deposit chain and are exiled to a reputation tundra, frozen out of high-value contracts until they re-earn standing through verifiable solo work.
